result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A gives a tight, buildable spec: a clear table of widths, a fixed source order, em breakpoints with a reason (zoom), a capped and centered layout for very wide screens, and starter CSS a developer can use directly. B covers more ground, with an explicit 'set breakpoints where the layout breaks' rule, a content-based reason for dropping the ad column at 1280px, and planned treatment for the wide-screen side margins. But B is long, reads more like general advice than a spec, and has no CSS sketch. A explains its breakpoints less in terms of when content stops fitting, but it is the more usable handoff for a developer. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put the recipe first on phones, cap the width on very wide screens and set phone padding. B is tighter and easier to build from: it uses two em-based breakpoints, a container query for the ingredients/method split, and working starter CSS that sets the exact column sizes and the cap. A covers more ground, including cook mode, print styles and ad-skin options, but it is long, has no CSS sketch and names its breakpoints after devices even though it says the developer should adjust them to the content.
